name: Earth Monitoring Benchmark
description: Recent progress in self-supervision shows that pre-training large neural networks on vast amounts of unsupervised data can lead to impressive increases in generalisation for downstream tasks. Such models, recently coined as foundation models, have been transformational to the field of natural language processing. While similar models have also been trained on large corpuses of images, they are not well suited for remote sensing data. To stimulate the development of foundation models for Earth monitoring, we propose to develop a new benchmark comprised of a variety of downstream tasks related to climate change. We believe that this can lead to substantial improvements in many existing applications and facilitate the development of new applications. This proposal is also a call for collaboration with the aim of developing a better evaluation process to mitigate potential downsides of foundation models for Earth monitoring.
evaluation_method: task-specific (accuracy / IoU / mAP / F1 / RMSE), often reported as a composite or per-task metric
general_score_metric: task-specific metrics aggregated into a composite score (when reported)
reputation: A proposal and emerging benchmark in the remote sensing / climate community intended to drive foundation-model development for Earth monitoring; growing interest but not yet a standardized community-wide standard.
notes: Heterogeneous tasks with differing evaluation metrics; potential geographic and temporal contamination risks; not an LLM benchmark (vision/remote-sensing focused); evaluation and metric aggregation are still being standardized across tasks.
